title: Faith and the Flag
subtitle: When the cross gets conscripted — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For the reader in a church that has started to sound like a campaign, and for the one who suspects their own side is not innocent either.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Start with the whole diagnosis, then trace the fusion back through its parts — the flag in the sanctuary, the persecution we invented, the pledge we forgot we could not make twice.

items.label: The State of the American Church
items.blurb: The whole diagnosis first: two captivities, right and left, and the older faith underneath both.

items.label: When God Bless America Replaces Thy Kingdom Come
items.blurb: How patriotism became the practical savior of American Christianity.

items.label: Why Is There a Flag in the Sanctuary?
items.blurb: It did not arrive by accident, and it does not stay there by accident.

items.label: Is the American Church Really Being Persecuted?
items.blurb: How comfort learned to call itself a cross.

items.label: Can You Pledge Allegiance to Two Kingdoms?
items.blurb: What allegiance to a crucified King costs when the nation asks first.

movements.heading: Then work the study
movements.note: Christian Nationalism is a five-session study that names what it is and is not, indicts every tribe by the same cross, and refuses to hand the sanctuary to a flag.

items.label: Christian Nationalism — a study
items.blurb: Five even-handed sessions for a room that will hear politics in every line.

movements.heading: Then read the book, free
movements.note: The Captive Church follows the one temptation Jesus refused in the wilderness through Constantine, the denarius, and the flag on the platform. Read it free.

items.label: The Captive Church — read free
items.blurb: Ten chapters on nationalism, empire, and the cost of cultural Christianity. The complete book, free.

items.blurb: Print and ebook editions of the full library.
